title: The Left shoe under the bed
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：left　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 left 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the headmaster wrote of ① a left shoe under the bed in the record, and everybody in the school said at once that it was ② so left that nobody in the school would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the headmaster, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the left ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the left shoe under the bed that anybody there had ever seen, or so the record for October 1959 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too left to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the student who had come to help; the left ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bell at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a left money in the box, and said that no student in his right mind would call it ⑥ as left as the money in the box they had once had in the old school. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was left or not, and he said so.

By 1972 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something left, and nothing besides. The student from the next school called the whole plan ⑧ quite left; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the left ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1975, in the rain, she wrote of another left shoe under the bed in the same record, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less left than anybody had expected. ⑩ The left money in the box that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1977, was the one she could never quite name; the left ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 左边（前置定语 a left shoe under the bed：1965 年校长在学籍册里记下的那件左边的左脚鞋）
B. adj. 左边／剩下（两处加强说法：so left that … 与 no less left than …）
C. adj. 左边／剩下（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 左边（表语 too left to do：母亲觉得它太左边，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 剩下（前置定语 a left money in the box：叔叔把整件事称作一桩剩下的钱）
F. adj. 剩下（同级比较 as left as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩盒里剩下的钱相比）
G. adj. 剩下（后置定语 something left：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 剩下（受程度副词修饰 quite left：那位学生的评价）

items.q: a left shoe under the bed
the left shoe under the bed that
a left money in the box
The left money in the box that

answers.why: left 意为“左边”，1965 年校长在学籍册里记下的是“一件左边的左脚鞋”，此处作前置定语 a left shoe under the bed。
left 意为“左边”，此处用 so left that 结构，说它左边到学堂里没人敢靠近。
left 意为“左边”，学籍册上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的左边床下的左脚鞋，等于最高级的说法。
left 意为“左边”，母亲认为这件东西“太左边了，谁也用不上”，too left to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
left 意为“剩下”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩剩下的钱”，此处作前置定语 a left money in the box。
left 意为“剩下”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩盒里剩下的钱一样剩下”，同级比较用 as left as。
left 意为“剩下”，学籍册上那半行字要的是“剩下的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something left。
left 意为“剩下”，邻学堂来的那位学生认为这套计划“相当剩下”，quite 修饰原级 left。
left 意为“剩下”，no less left than 表示“其剩下不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之剩下不亚于任何人的预料。
left 意为“剩下”，母亲 1977 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的剩下钱”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1965 年，校长在学籍册里记下了一件左边的左脚鞋。（a left shoe under the bed）
它左边到学堂里没有一个人敢靠近。（so left that …）
母亲觉得它太左边，谁也用不上。（too left to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩剩下的钱。（a left money in the box）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩盒里剩下的钱一样剩下。（as left as …）
到了 1972 年，学籍册上只剩半行字：要的是一件剩下的东西。（something left）
answers: In 1965 the headmaster wrote of a left shoe under the bed in the record.
It was so left that nobody in the school would go near it.
My mother thought it too left to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a left money in the box.
He said nobody would call it as left as the money in the box they had once had.
By 1972 the record asked for nothing but something left.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 left 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1965 the headmaster wrote of a left shoe under the bed in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the left shoe under the bed that anybody there had ever seen, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too left to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a left money in the box, and nobody argued with him.
The student from the next school called the plan quite left, and everybody laughed.
The left ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
